prompt: Review this anchor as its assigned subagent. Enumerate ALL requirements, qualifications, edge cases and scenarios. Inspect all supplied implementation and test fragments and trace each aspect to implementation behavior and actual test assertions or justified TODO/N/A evidence. Passing tests and associations alone are insufficient. Follow helpers and capture every additional source dependency with cargo meta review read ANCHOR PATH [selector] before completing the report. Explain prerequisites for justified TODO tests; do not claim deferred behavior is implemented. Distinguish source inspection from commands actually executed. Write a JSON report containing reviewer, report, and requested_edits. Leave requested_edits empty only when every aspect is accounted for and no edits are needed. Otherwise list concrete changes, including missing tests or justified TODO tests with prerequisite comments. Run cargo meta review record ANCHOR REPORT_FILE to finish. After edits or stale-input rejection, run cargo meta review start ANCHOR and review the fresh inputs. The gate fails until a current report with no requested edits is recorded. Dependency capture is agent-declared.
coordinator_instructions: Review only your assigned anchor using the sage-review-checklist skill and its start/read/record workflow. Capture these instructions with start --instructions /tmp/anchor-review-instructions.txt. Use captured source context; do not import old approvals or uncaptured coordinator conclusions. Write only your anchor's validations directory and a unique report file under /tmp. Coordinate production, test, and association edits with the coordinator before making them because concurrent reviewers may capture the same files. Capture essential dependencies using review read; report any necessary association additions for coordinated handling. Existing TODO/N/A evidence must be individually justified and remain deferred; do not claim passing placeholders verify functionality. Distinguish source review from tests actually run. On a suspected behavioral violation, coordinate a regression test and follow the skill rather than rubber-stamping. Return a concise summary of the recorded outcome or precise unresolved finding. Do not commit or change unrelated files.

A validation records an agent's assessment of one specification anchor against
its implementation and tests. The saved context lets `cargo meta` check whether
that assessment still applies. Running tests remains a separate obligation.
The main agent discovers review work through a failing `cargo meta check` or
the shared Cargo validation test. Diagnostics identify the affected anchors,
explain why they need review, and direct the agent to the review skill. The
skill delegates one subagent per anchor, supplying its ID and an initial prompt.
The subagent obtains its source context through the review commands, so that
the saved inputs are the same inputs it consumes.
participant Check as Check / Cargo validation test
participant Reviewer as Review subagent (one per anchor)
participant CLI as cargo meta review
Check-->>Main: Fail: affected anchors, reasons, review skill
Main->>Reviewer: Follow skill, review anchor using initial prompt
CLI->>Files: Clear old validation, save summary and initial inputs
Note over Check,Files: No output exists: the gate must fail
CLI-->>Reviewer: Print the saved inputs and verification prompt
CLI->>Files: Append the selected source fragment
CLI-->>Reviewer: Return the exact saved contents
CLI->>CLI: Verify freshness and report format
alt Inputs changed or report invalid
CLI-->>Reviewer: Reject recording, gate still fails
CLI->>Files: Save output and recording time, preserve inputs
Reviewer-->>Main: Report results and any requested edits
alt Every anchor has a current report with no requested edits
else Missing, unfinished, stale, or changes requested
Note over Main,Reviewer: Resolve edits and repeat review for affected anchors
The subagent captures inputs and records its report in the validation directory
created by `start`. Starting a review removes its previous output even when the
source has not changed, so an interrupted review cannot reuse an old approval.
Each additional read is saved before its contents are returned. Recording
checks the captured inputs for freshness and preserves them exactly.
A successful `record` is necessary but does not by itself make the gate pass.
The report must request no edits, its inputs must still be current, and every
other anchor must also satisfy the gate. If edits are requested, the main agent
coordinates them and starts fresh reviews for affected anchors. An accepted
review of justified TODO/N/A evidence leaves that status visible; it does not
claim the deferred behavior is implemented.

Claim, implementation, and annotated test source snapshots are stored in `input.json` as
arrays of source lines. Joining an array with newline characters recovers the

`Selector::WholeFile` selects all contents of the fragment's source file,
including any trailing newline. It carries no additional selector data.
`Selector::LineRange { start, end }` selects a one-based, inclusive range of
lines within the fragment's source file. Lines are delimited by `\n`; selected
text retains the original line endings, including the last selected line's
ending if present. Zero, reversed, or out-of-bounds ranges are invalid.
The saved line numbers are used again when checking freshness, so shifting
content across those boundaries may conservatively make the fragment stale.

`Selector::Test { crate_name, target, rust_path }` selects the complete annotated
Rust test function within the fragment's source file, including attributes,

## Versioned egraph children are inference transactions
Operations that may partially constrain inference state run in a child egraph
version. On complete success, a short-lived probe may collapse its child into
the direct parent; on failure, it discards the child, so partial equalities,
bounds, and wake effects cannot escape. The probe API permits collapse only
when the probe is the parent's only live child, so no sibling can observe its
parent changing underneath an in-progress computation.
Concurrent alternatives are different: each candidate owns an isolated proof
context and performs its speculative matching in a child version of that
context. Candidate versions are never merged into a requester. Each candidate
extracts a canonical response before its isolated context is dropped, so no
alternative-specific choice can become another candidate's ancestor state.
Because descendants read sparse state through their ancestry, per-version
writes target leaf versions only. Creating a child freezes its parent until
every child is discarded or the sole child is atomically collapsed; read-only
lookup from the frozen parent is allowed, but path compression, variable
allocation, equality/bound changes, rebuild publication, semantic revisions,
and wake publication are not. Append-only allocation in the proof context's
shared `Stash` is the sole non-version fact exempt from this rule. This gives
each branch a stable ancestor snapshot without copying the parent maps.
